- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.00) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — consider slight upward correction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overcorrects downward; reduce forecast decline magnitude by 10–20% in next period.  
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model tends to underestimate — adjust forecast upward slightly.  
- If forecast is flat or slowly rising but true outcome shows strong upward momentum, consider adding 2–3% upward bias to next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), forecast should not be overly aggressive — use historical mean as baseline.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid linear extrapolation — model often misses volatility clustering; add 1–2% smoothing or volatility buffer.
